beats.text: Step one. Choose the candidate pair. This is a guided reconstruction of the DECOUPLE workbench, using states captured from the real engine.
The extract abundances, parasite inhibition and host-cell toxicity are real archived measurements. The probabilities and verdicts are model outputs.
Open the candidate menu and choose the methyl xanthone at mass 353 and the rotenoid at mass 393. These are annotation candidates, not confirmed structures.
Read the left panel. After the starting assays, rotenoid alone holds 39.7 percent, and both together 60.3. The current evidence cannot separate them.
Step two. Inspect the recommendation before spending an assay. The sample table shows the abundance of each candidate.
Scroll down to the baseline. Strongest-first would choose another rotenoid-rich extract because it predicts the largest response.
Now return to the recommended row. DECOUPLE chooses Uncarina decaryi green stems. It carries the xanthone, with no detected rotenoid.
Read the predicted responses. Under the xanthone explanation, about 0.99. Under the rotenoid explanation, about 0.05. That gap makes this a useful contrast.
Step three. Click Reveal assay. In this retrospective demo, the button uncovers an archived measurement. In a prospective study, this is where the laboratory would run the assay.
The row now shows both readouts: parasite inhibition 0.001, and host toxicity 0.022. Inactive.
Watch the model update. Support for the rotenoid alone rises from 39.7 to 99.9 percent. This is conditional model support, not a confirmed causal identity. Two assays remain.
Read the next recommendation, then reveal assay two. Another xanthone-only extract is inactive.
One assay remains. Reveal the third recommendation. It is also inactive. The budget is now zero. These are three separate archived observations.
Step four. Click Finalize decision after all three reveals.
The model nominates the rotenoid, and the toxicity model does not flag it. This is a hypothesis. The next experimental step is a purified-compound assay.

Next, click Compare with strongest-first. Both policies have the same budget and archived outcomes. In this one example, strongest-first ends with a shortlist: the joint explanation or the rotenoid. This example does not establish that adaptive contrast is better overall.
Finally, export the JSON decision trace. It records the observations and decisions for review. The workflow is choose, inspect, reveal, finalize, compare, and export.
